goal: Mime.getType(path) (src/Mime.ts) derives a type from the extension after the last dot of the last path segment. The two regular expressions that strip the directory part and the part before the extension do not match across line terminators, so a file name that contains one is typed wrongly: getType('LINE\nFEED.png') returns null instead of 'image/png', and the same happens for a carriage return (U+000D), a line separator (U+2028) and a paragraph separator (U+2029), with or without a directory part in front. This matters where the file name comes from an untrusted source: a content type decided from it must come from the extension after the last dot of the last segment, whatever characters precede it, so that a name crafted with a line terminator cannot make the lookup fail or pick an earlier extension. Make getType treat every line terminator like any other character when it strips the directory part and the extension's prefix; a space or tab in the name already works and must keep working. getExtension, define and the rest of the class stay as they are. The change belongs in src/Mime.ts only. Repository rules: keep the file's existing style, no new dependencies, no edits under test or types, and the whole suite (npm test, which builds first) must keep passing.

goal: A tar entry's size comes from the 12-byte size field of its header block (octal, or base-256 for large and negative numbers), from a pax extended header's 'size' record, or from a global extended header. Nothing stops any of them from being negative, and a negative size makes the reader miscount the bytes that follow the header. Refuse negative sizes in src/header.ts and src/pax.ts. In the Header class: when a block is decoded, the size it computes (the extended header's size, else the global extended header's size, else the block's own size field) becomes undefined if it is negative; and header data whose size is negative when compared as a number, whether passed to the constructor (new Header({ size: -1000 })) or merged in from an extended header, is ignored, so header.size stays undefined. In Pax.parse, a 'size' record is kept only when its numeric value is zero or greater: 'size=-1000' and a non-numeric value leave size undefined, while 'size=1000' gives 1000 and 'size=0' gives 0. Every other field (uid, gid, mode, the times and so on) keeps its current parsing, negative values included, and nothing else changes. Change only src/header.ts and src/pax.ts; do not edit tests. The tests import the built dist, so build with npm run prepare (tshy and an esbuild bundle) before running them; npm test runs prepare and then tap. The suite's assertions must keep passing: npm test -- --allow-incomplete-coverage (tap's 100% coverage rule already fails at the current commit on one branch of src/pax.ts, so it is not a rule here).
